Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed last week, after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel . Ukraine then accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support. Trump and Zelensky have since exchanged sharp words about one another. clusters.snippet: The White House is facing growing adversity, writes the BBC's Anthony Zurcher, weeks before crucial midterm elections.

clusters.text: The political strategist was a frequent fixture on conservative Newsmax and Fox News before her appointment The White House press secretary job is a challenging one, even under the best of circumstances. Katie Zacharia was thrown into the whirlwind, joining the White House team as press secretary just weeks away from what polls suggest could be a difficult midterm congressional elections for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. In just five days, she was out – the result of a disastrous press conference that lasted all of 14 minutes, followed by a series of halting media appearances and questions about whether she had mischaracterised her legal credentials over the course of her career. The axe dropped on Friday, with the news delivered – in a roundabout way - by Trump himself before the gathered media at the White House, as he recounted a conversation he had with Zacharia earlier in the day. "Honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider," Trump said he told Zacharia. "Katie, do you need this? I don't think you need this." He later added that maybe the press secretary job "is not for her". In case there was any doubt, the White House quickly confirmed to the BBC that Zacharia would be "transitioning" out of her current job. Watch: The BBC's Sarah Smith on what went wrong for Katie Zacharia Trump may be wondering whether Zacharia "needs" the press secretary job, but presidents – including this one - benefit most from a competent press secretary in times of crisis. And while there may not be an immediate crisis, this White House is certainly facing growing adversity. Across the US, Republican candidates are scrambling to hold on to their seats in the upcoming elections. Some are doing so by distancing themselves from the president and his policies, creating new stresses and faultlines within a party that has for so long been broadly unified behind Trump. Meanwhile, the White House has been beset by a series of controversies – including allegations of corruption that forced the resignation of US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and an abrupt reversal of plans to publicly air a military execution in December after widespread bipartisan backlash. A skilled press secretary may have been able to navigate these political landmines while continuing to push out the White House's preferred message in the face of a building media frenzy. clusters.text: SENIOR BJP leader and former deputy prime minister Lal Krishna Advani was admitted to Apollo Hospital in the Capital on Friday evening with a chest infection. He was brought to the hospital around 7.30 pm, said hospital officials. He has been admitted to the pulmonary department and is under observation by a team of doctors. Tests are underway, said the officials. The 98-year-old leader was last admitted to Apollo in May this year due to age-related health complications. He was discharged after a few days. Advani is among the architects of the modern BJP. He was party president for three terms — 1986 to 1990, 1993 to 1998 and 2004 to 2005. On September 25, 1990, he set out on his Ram Rath Yatra from Somnath, a campaign that brought the Ram Temple movement from the margins to the centre of national politics. His yatra was halted following his arrest in Samastipur, Bihar, on October 23 that year. On December 6, 1992, the Babri Masjid was demolished in Ayodhya. Years later, a special CBI court acquitted him and other accused in the demolition case. In the NDA government led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Advani was Union Home Minister from 1998 to 2004, and Deputy Prime Minister from 2002 to 2004. The 1999 Kargil conflict and the 2001 attack on Parliament happened during his time in the Home Ministry. Advani also served as Information and Broadcasting Minister in the Morarji Desai government from 1977 to 1979. In 2024, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna, the country's highest civilian honour.

Apple updates App Review Guidelines to crack down on AI nudify apps and apps that reveal undocumented capabilities, like nudification, after app review (Marcus Mendes/9to5Mac)
clusters.text: Apple’s App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called “nudify” apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools. The rule changes follow significant criticism toward Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes, including minors. Apple didn’t pull X or Grok from the App Store, though it told senators that it threatened to yank Grok. At Apple’s WWDC event in June, protestors also called on Apple to “remove Grok, X, and all nudify technology from the App Store,” and in July, a San Francisco city attorney ordered Apple to remove 13 “nudify” apps, which it said it did. As part of updates announced Friday, Apple says that developers “must proactively prevent and remove” nonconsensual, sexual images as part of its content moderation requirements for App Store apps. Developers who “fail to implement adequate safeguards” or “don’t remedy violations after notice” may be removed from the App Store. Apple also clarified a rule that bars “bait-and-switch” apps, or apps that add or change features, including “nudification,” after they have been approved. Apple’s rules also more clearly spell out that any apps that “facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children” will be pulled from the App Store and “blocked from alternative distribution.”

clusters.text: New Delhi: Park Hospital, part of Park Medi World Limited, marked the groundbreaking ceremony for its upcoming 550-bed multi-super-speciality hospital in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. With an investment of approximately Rs. 200 crore, the project represents a significant step in the Group's expansion plans and its efforts to strengthen healthcare infrastructure in the region. The hospital is being developed under a public-private partnership (PPP) with the Prayagraj Municipal Corporation. The project is expected to expand access to organised, multi-speciality healthcare for residents of Prayagraj and neighbouring areas. The facility is targeted for completion within two years from the appointed date under the concession agreement.Also Read:Park Medi World to acquire Medicity Hospital in Rudrapur for Rs 177 croreThe groundbreaking marks the next stage of a project for which Park Medi World received the PPP mandate in August 2026. clusters.text: American Express is changing how Membership Rewards points are pooled across cards in India and the US. While the mechanics differ between the two markets, the direction of travel is worth watching. One reason I have always liked American Express Membership Rewards is its simplicity. You earn points across eligible cards, accumulate them in a common pool, and decide later how you want to use them. You could earn points on one card, add to your balance with another, and eventually transfer the combined total to an airline or hotel loyalty programme. It was a straightforward proposition. You earned Membership Rewards points, not points that needed to be treated differently depending on which American Express card you used to earn them. That simplicity is now being challenged on both sides of the world. clusters.text: Prayagraj: The Allahabad High Court has granted bail to an accused in the 2020 Bikru massacre in Kanpur on the ground that other similarly placed co-accused have already been released on bail.The accused, Ram Singh, worked as the driver of the main accused Vikas Dubey.On the night of July 2, 2020, at least eight police personnel, including deputy superintendent of police Devendra Mishra, were killed by gangster Vikas Dubey in an ambush when the police team raided his house in Kanpur’s Bikru village to arrest him.Vikas Dubey was killed on July 10, 2020, when he tried to escape custody after a police vehicle bringing him to Kanpur from Ujjain met with an accident.A criminal case against Ram Singh was registered at Chaubeypur police station in Kanpur on charges of murder and attempt to murder.Granting bail to the accused on Oct 13, Justice Krishan Pahal observed, “The criminal history assigned to the applicant has been explained except one case under the UP Gangsters Act. clusters.text: Sonay Kartal has dropped to 170 in the world after her long-term injury, but reached a career-high ranking of 44 in July 2025 Sonay Kartal had a difficult decision to make when she felt ready to rejoin the WTA Tour, having not played for six months because of a debilitating back injury. Did the 24-year-old Briton ease herself in more gently at lower-ranked tournaments? Or did the former world number 54 use a protected injury ranking to enter WTA 1000 events in China, where the world's best players compete at the pinnacle of the women's tour? Kartal chose the latter option - and it is paying off handsomely. On Friday, she beat world number six Elina Svitolina at the Wuhan Open to reach the first WTA 1000 semi-final of her career. "I didn't expect to be back at this level this quickly – I don't think many people did," Kartal said. "I knew it would be a tough choice. I didn't know how I was going to be on the match court – it's very easy to train well but the match scenario is completely different. "I decided to throw myself in the deep end and play the best players in the world. Patience has been paramount for Kartal, who announced herself to the wider British public by reaching the fourth round at Wimbledon last year, as she dealt with a stress fracture in her back. Kartal had earned impressive victories over 2025 Australian Open champion Madison Keys and 2024 US Open semi-finalist Emma Navarro at Indian Wells in March, but was forced to retire from a fourth-round meeting with now world number one Elena Rybakina. The issue proved more serious than first thought, leading to the longest absence from competitive action of Kartal's career. But she has returned to the WTA Tour playing like she has never been away. Known for her consistent hitting from the baseline, supreme athleticism and tenacity, Kartal added Ukraine's Svitolina to her list of high-profile victories in Wuhan with a 6-2 2-6 6-4 triumph. Kartal beat Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini - a Wimbledon and French Open finalist in 2024 - in the last 16, backing up the win over Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic - who won the Tokyo Olympic title in 2021 - in the second round.
